frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #10: 'Add storage ports that return typed available, not_provisioned, corrupt and unavailable results; production callers must fail closed on any non-available state.' -- implemented as SecureStorageStatus (4 states) plus secure_storage_get_u32/get_str/get_blob typed read wrappers and a single reusable secure_storage_fail_closed_pass() predicate every production call site should gate on.

S5's 'Contracts and invariants' text: 'Secure-storage failure returns secure_storage_unavailable and maps to HTTP 503 when exposed later.' -- SecureStorageStatus::kUnavailable is the direct implementation of this named failure mode; the HTTP 503 mapping itself is out of scope for this sub-slice (no HTTP route consumes this port yet -- that is S6/later work) but the typed value it will map from now exists.

This sub-slice builds directly on Section 2.7's namespace ownership registry (plan #9/#15, prior sub-slice) rather than duplicating key-ownership knowledge: every read is gated by find_owning_namespace_for_key() before touching hal_nvs at all, both catching a real defect class (wrong-namespace call sites) and satisfying plan #10's own fail-closed mandate for that case too.

typed_status_and_classification.detail: SecureStorageStatus{kAvailable, kNotProvisioned, kCorrupt, kUnavailable}. secure_storage_classify_raw_status() maps the 4 hal_nvs_status_t values that matter: HAL_NVS_STATUS_OK -> kAvailable; HAL_NVS_STATUS_NOT_FOUND -> kNotProvisioned; HAL_NVS_STATUS_NO_SPACE -> kCorrupt (stored value does not fit the caller's declared buffer -- a size/schema mismatch signal); HAL_NVS_STATUS_ERR/HAL_NVS_STATUS_INVALID_ARG -> kUnavailable (storage-subsystem-level problem). secure_storage_downgrade_to_corrupt_if_invalid() lets a caller with its own fixed-layout schema (magic number/version/checksum) downgrade a tentative kAvailable to kCorrupt after inspecting the actual bytes, without this generic port needing to know any consumer's specific schema.

fail_closed_predicate.detail: secure_storage_fail_closed_pass(status) is true only for kAvailable -- implements plan #10's 'production callers must fail closed on any non-available state' as one small, reusable, directly-testable function rather than leaving every future call site to hand-roll the same comparison (and risk drifting from the contract, e.g. accidentally treating kNotProvisioned as acceptable for a secret read).

namespace_gated_typed_reads.detail: secure_storage_get_u32/get_str/get_blob(namespace_id, key, ...) each call Section 2.7's find_owning_namespace_for_key(key) first and return kUnavailable immediately -- without ever calling hal_nvs -- if the key does not belong to the claimed namespace (covering null/empty/entirely-unknown keys too). Verified this short-circuit actually prevents the underlying hal_nvs call and leaves the caller's output buffer/value untouched by pre-filling with a sentinel and asserting it survives unchanged.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Matches this document's established per-item sub-slicing discipline (each of S5's ten 'Encrypted storage foundation' items builds on the ones before it; #10 itself was scoped this way explicitly per the user's own prior selection of '#9-18' being split into foundation-first sub-slices). deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No existing production code path (config_manager, connectivity_manager, matter_endpoint_registry, etc.) calls secure_storage_get_* yet -- they still call hal_nvs_get_* directly. This port exists and is fully tested but is not yet load-bearing for any real read. Wiring real call sites to it, or building #11's migration/#12's write gate on top, is future work.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The four-state classification only distinguishes storage-subsystem-level problems (kUnavailable) from a size/shape mismatch (kCorrupt) using the existing hal_nvs_status_t vocabulary (HAL_NVS_STATUS_ERR/INVALID_ARG vs. HAL_NVS_STATUS_NO_SPACE); it cannot distinguish e.g. 'flash hardware read error' from 'NVS Encryption key unavailable' from 'generic ESP-IDF NVS internal error' -- hal_nvs.c itself does not currently surface that distinction at the per-call level.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Redesigning hal_nvs.c's own status vocabulary to carry finer-grained subsystem-failure detail is a larger, separate change than this sub-slice's scope (typed results layered on top of the existing HAL contract, not a HAL redesign) and was not requested.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Every storage-subsystem-level failure this port can currently observe collapses to a single kUnavailable value regardless of root cause; a future consumer wanting to distinguish 'NVS Encryption not yet verified active' (plan #12's concern) from 'raw flash error' will need hal_nvs.c itself to expose that distinction first.
